verdict: Leads are flowing at strong cost, but peak-season delays need closing now.
narrative: In the last 28 days you received 33 leads from Meta at a cost of $47.15 per lead — a sharp improvement over the prior period — while Google Ads recorded 12 additional conversions. The surge was concentrated in mid-October (Oct 16–18), and the most recent days show lead flow cooling back toward a steadier pace, so this week's numbers should be read in that context. Nine planned milestones are currently overdue, including the heating campaigns, LSA re-enable, and fall creative package, all of which were scheduled to launch before the heating season opened; those are being escalated and pushed to completion now. On the intake side, the volume of contacts entering your CRM does not yet match the lead count from ads, which points to a gap in how incoming leads are being captured and followed up — this is being addressed directly. Expect tighter lead tracking and the first heating-season assets to come online in the days ahead.

highlights.phrase: leads received this period via Meta, at $47.15 each — your lowest cost per lead to date
planned milestones now overdue, including heating campaigns that missed the start of peak season
total actions on your Google Business profiles this period — calls, direction requests, and website clicks

watch_item.issue: Leads entering your CRM are not fully matching the leads recorded from ads, meaning some incoming inquiries may not be getting followed up.
watch_item.fix: The intake and lead-routing process is being audited and corrected so every lead is captured and assigned without gaps.
